name: Lab Intelligence Agent
description: Universal health data normalizer and interpreter for functional medicine. Ingests lab results, wearable data, and genomic data from ANY source and format — HL7v2, FHIR, C-CDA, CSV, PDF text, Apple Health, Oura, Withings, Garmin, Fitbit, WHOOP, Dexcom, 23andMe, VCF — normalizes everything to LOINC-coded standards, and interprets through a functional medicine lens with pattern detection, trending, and follow-up recommendations.

skills.name: Universal Health Data Ingestion
skills.description: Auto-detect and ingest ANY health data format. Supports 15+ formats including HL7v2, FHIR R4, C-CDA XML, Apple Health XML, Oura/Withings/Garmin/Fitbit/WHOOP/Dexcom wearable data, 23andMe/AncestryDNA/VCF genomic files, Rupa Health labs, CSV exports from any lab company, and raw text from PDFs or screenshots.
examples: Here are my patient's lab results from Quest
Parse this HL7 message from our lab interface
Import this Apple Health export
Analyze this 23andMe raw data file
What format is this data?

skills.name: Functional Medicine Lab Interpretation
skills.description: Interpret lab results using functional medicine optimal reference ranges — tighter than conventional ranges to catch dysfunction early. Covers 120+ biomarkers across thyroid, metabolic, lipids, inflammation, iron, nutrients, liver, kidney, CBC, hormones, adrenal, gut, cardiac, autoimmune, and more.
examples: Interpret these thyroid results with functional ranges
Is this TSH of 3.8 actually optimal?
Flag anything outside functional medicine ranges
Compare conventional vs functional interpretation

skills.name: Clinical Pattern Recognition
skills.description: Detect multi-biomarker clinical patterns: thyroid conversion issues, Hashimoto's, insulin resistance, iron deficiency (with/without anemia), methylation dysfunction, chronic inflammation, HPA axis dysregulation, PCOS, metabolic syndrome, anemia differential, liver dysfunction patterns, and gut-immune axis dysfunction.
examples: What patterns do you see in these results?
Is there an insulin resistance pattern here?
Check for thyroid conversion issues
Cross-reference these labs for hidden patterns

skills.name: Genomic Variant Analysis
skills.description: Parse and interpret consumer genomic data (23andMe, AncestryDNA) and clinical VCF files. Covers 30+ clinically relevant SNPs: MTHFR, COMT, CBS, CYP450 pharmacogenomics, VDR, HFE, APOE, Factor V Leiden, and more. Generates methylation profiles, pharmacogenomic metabolizer status, and lab test recommendations based on variants.
examples: Analyze my 23andMe raw data
What does my MTHFR status mean for my labs?
Check for drug metabolism variants
What labs should I order based on my genetics?

skills.name: Cross-Source Biomarker Trending
skills.description: Track biomarkers over time regardless of which lab, EHR, or device the data came from. Handles mixed sources (Quest via FHIR + Rupa + manual entry) with automatic unit normalization. Detects whether trends are moving toward or away from functional optimal.
examples: Show me this patient's Vitamin D trend over the last year
Has their thyroid been improving?
Compare these two lab panels 6 months apart
Trend their ferritin from three different lab sources

skills.name: Follow-Up Test Recommendations
skills.description: Based on current results and detected patterns, suggest additional tests to complete the clinical picture. Uses related-marker cross-references and pattern logic to identify gaps.
examples: What should I order next based on these results?
We're missing some thyroid markers — which ones?
What follow-up labs does this pattern suggest?

skills.name: Lab-Wearable Data Correlation
skills.description: Correlate wearable device metrics (HRV, sleep, glucose, activity, body composition) with lab results for a holistic health picture. Maps wearable data to LOINC codes where applicable.
examples: Compare their Oura sleep data with their cortisol levels
Their HRV is declining — what do the labs show?
Correlate CGM glucose patterns with their HbA1c
